tasks.title: Ignore rules, file types, and glob strategies in ripgrep
tasks.initialPrompt: Audit how ripgrep decides which files to search, across the directory walker, ignore-file handling, the default file types, and glob matching. Record each of these facts in evidence.md on its own line as `key: value`, with a bare integer for numeric values, and keep every such line present whenever you rewrite the file: `walker-fallback-threads` (the thread count the parallel walker uses when its configured count is zero), `ts-glob-count` (the number of globs in the default `ts` file type), `py-second-glob` (the second glob of the default `py` file type), `glob-strategy-count` (the number of variants of the per-glob match strategy enum in the globset crate), `global-excludes-function` (the public function that resolves git's global excludes file), `excludes-default-function` (the private function that supplies the fallback path when git's configuration names no excludes file), and `own-ignore-file` (the ignore file name that ripgrep's own argument layer registers with the walker). Begin by locating those modules, then read crates/ignore/src/walk.rs, crates/ignore/src/dir.rs, crates/ignore/src/gitignore.rs, crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs, crates/ignore/src/types.rs, crates/ignore/src/overrides.rs, crates/globset/src/glob.rs, and crates/globset/src/lib.rs completely, in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines, and then the walker-related parts of crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs. Explain the precedence between ignore sources, how parent directories are consulted, and which glob shapes avoid the regex engine. Read substantial source and test ranges, rather than answering from a directory listing or remembered knowledge. After recording the requested facts, investigate related edge cases and tests in tests/feature.rs and tests/regression.rs until the runner stops live work. Use only repository tools; do not use web tools or execute builds or tests. Do not modify repository source files, tests, or configuration. Write your findings and source citations to evidence.md using the artifact tools. Repeat the requested verified paths, names, and values in your final answer. Continue checking concrete source and test evidence until the runner asks you to stop live work.

tasks.title: List limits and polling intervals across gh command families
tasks.initialPrompt: Audit the result limits and polling intervals that GitHub CLI command families apply by default. Record each of these facts in evidence.md on its own line as `key: value`, with a bare integer for numeric values, and keep every such line present whenever you rewrite the file: `run-list-limit` (default number of workflow runs `gh run list` fetches), `workflow-list-limit` (default for `gh workflow list`), `gist-list-limit` (default for `gh gist list`), `run-delete-lookup` (how many recent runs `gh run delete` fetches when it has to prompt), `run-watch-interval-seconds` (default refresh interval of `gh run watch`), `pr-checks-interval-seconds` (default refresh interval of `gh pr checks` in watch mode), and `project-limit-max` (the maximum item limit declared by the shared project queries). Also report the name of the constant that bounds the run-delete lookup. Begin by locating those commands, then read the list, view, watch, and delete commands under pkg/cmd/run together with pkg/cmd/run/shared, the commands under pkg/cmd/workflow, pkg/cmd/gist/list and pkg/cmd/gist/shared, pkg/cmd/pr/checks, and pkg/cmd/project/shared/queries/queries.go completely, in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Explain how each command pages through the API once the limit exceeds one page and where a limit is validated.
